thread_a.role: MACsec RX handler on one CPU

thread_b.role: MACsec RX/TX handler on another CPU (same handler, self-race)

emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([rmw(netdev->stats.<counter>)]) from thread_a (the ++ read-modify-write of a per-device stats counter must not interleave with a conflicting RMW of the SAME counter)
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@macsec_handle_frame:1233 = mutate(netdev->stats.<counter>++) on another CPU (same counter)
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: plain C '++' on dev->stats is a non-atomic read-modify-write; nothing serializes the per-device stats across the multiple packet-processing CPUs (no lock, no atomic op) → no g establishes atomic(rmw)
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic over a single RMW access; a concurrent conflicting RMW of the same counter → lost-update data race

fix_maps_to: plain dev->stats.X++ replaced by DEV_STATS_INC(dev, X) (atomic_long_inc on the __X backing counter) and stats64 reads switched to atomic_long_read → makes each increment an atomic RMW → establishes atomic([rmw]) so the accesses no longer conflict
recall_risk_notes: Textbook non-atomic-counter self-race; our design models macsec_handle_frame as an rx_handler self-race root and the unprotected '++' yields atomic(single RMW) directly. Risks: (1) it is a benign lost-counter race, which an LLM may downrank/decline to assert (precision pressure causing FN); (2) the two GT-listed lines are DIFFERENT fields (rx_errors vs rx_dropped), so same_location grounding between exactly those two sites would fail — the true conflict is each counter racing with itself across CPUs, which the per-object session must capture.
